The present claim pertains to the alleged road traffic accident involving Salman Hasan (hereinafter referred to as the injured), who is stated to have suffered injuries due to the offending vehicle bearing Registration No. UP 14DC 8008. The said vehicle was being driven and owned by Md. Swarim (hereinafter referred to as Respondent No.1) and was insured with ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Respondent No.2). 2. Brief Facts as per DAR: (a) Preliminary information regarding the accident in question was received vide DD No. 103 dated 03.10.2023 by ASI Subhash Chand, who was on emergency duty. Upon receipt of the said information, he immediately reached the spot, where he found the offending vehicle bearing registration No. UP-14DC-8008 in an accidental condition. He was informed that the injured persons had already been removed to the hospital. In the meantime, the police officials met the complainant at the spot and recorded his statement. The complainant stated that on the date of the accident, he along with his uncle (chacha), namely Salman, was returning to their residence on foot after having meals at a hotel. At about 09.45 PM, when they reached near Pocket-12, Main Road, Jasola, New Delhi, alleged offending vehicle (Innova car), driven by its driver in a very rash and negligent manner, came MACT No. 567/2024 Salman Hasan Vs. Md Swarim & Ors. Page No. 2 of 27 (Ravi) from behind and hit both of them. As a result of the said impact, both sustained injuries. The complainant stated that he received minor injuries, whereas his uncle Salman sustained serious injuries. He further stated that after hitting both pedestrians, the offending vehicle also struck a Tempo bearing registration No. DL-1LAE-9777, which was parked on the side of the road. Thereafter, the driver of the offending vehicle attempted to flee from the spot but was apprehended by the complainant with the help of other public persons. The injured were taken to Alshifa Hospital by their known persons. Someone also made a call to the emergency number 112. Subsequently, the police apprehended the respondent/driver and seized the offending vehicle. The crime team was called at the spot, the site of the accident was inspected, and photographs were taken. Later, upon receipt of DD No. 133, the police officials obtained the MLC from Alshifa Hospital, wherein a brief history of the accident was recorded. On the basis of the description noted in the MLC, the FIR was registered. The medical examination of the driver/respondent no.1 was also conducted at ESI Hospital, wherein smell of alcohol was observed, and consequently, the relevant penal provision under the Motor Vehicles Act was added. Notice under Section 133 of the Motor Vehicles Act was served upon the driver of the offending vehicle, who replied in writing admitting that he was driving the said vehicle at the time of the accident. The documents pertaining to the offending vehicle were seized and verified and were later found to be in order. Mechanical inspection of the offending vehicle was also conducted. (b) During the course of investigation, the statement of the MACT No. 567/2024 Salman Hasan Vs. Md Swarim & Ors. He specifically denied the suggestion that he was crossing the road without using a zebra crossing. He also denied that he had suddenly come onto the road or that he had given insufficient time to the driver of the offending vehicle to apply brakes. Similar suggestions were put to PW-1 by the learned counsel for respondent no.1 (driver-cum- owner), which were also unequivocally denied. texts.arguments: (b) Learned counsel for the claimants submitted that the accident in question occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. It was contended that the said fact stands substantiated not only from the police record but also from the conduct of the driver of the offending vehicle, who himself admitted his involvement upon issuance of notice under Section 133 of the Motor Vehicles Act, thereby disclosing that he was driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time. It was further argued that as a result of the accident, the injured sustained serious injuries, due to which he remained under treatment and was unable to carry out his normal avocation for a considerable period. Learned counsel further contended that the entry "132/74" mentioned on medical report of driver cum owner, issued from ESI Hospital, Okhla, pertains to the blood pressure reading of the injured and not to the alcohol content. It was argued that the medical record has been misread by the claimants. It was also submitted that the notation "WNL" appearing in the document signifies "Within Normal/Permissible Limit" and has been used to demonstrate normal level of alcohol in blood negating any allegation regarding consumption of alcohol. (d) Learned counsel for the insurance company contended that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the victim himself. Learned counsel further submitted that driving or being present on the road under the influence of alcohol amounts to a violation of statutory norms, and therefore the insurance company cannot be saddled with liability. It was contended that such conduct constitutes a fundamental breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, absolving the insurer of its liability. The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. [See C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair [(1969) 3 SCC 64 : AIR 1970 MACT No. 567/2024 Salman Hasan Vs. Md Swarim & Ors. Page No. 15 of 27 (Ravi) SC 376] , R.D. Hattangadi v. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii)(a) and (iv).
